title: Tama, the station master cat
hook: A calico cat in a station master's cap helped rescue a small Japanese railway.
peek: In 2007 a small rural railway in Wakayama, Japan, appointed a calico cat named Tama as station master. Tourists came to see her, ridership rose, and a station was later rebuilt in the shape of a cat's face.
lede: By the mid-2000s, the little Kishigawa Line in Wakayama, Japan, was losing money and close to shutting. A new operator, Wakayama Electric Railway, took it over and made its stations unstaffed. At Kishi station lived Tama, a calico cat looked after by a local shop owner. In January 2007 the railway's president made her the official station master.

bullets.text: Tama was given a custom-made cap and a name badge, and she was paid in cat food. Her job was simply to sit at the ticket gate and greet passengers, which she did with great calm.
Visitors from across Japan and abroad began riding the line just to see her. Passenger numbers rose, and one economist estimated her fame brought about a billion yen to the local economy.
Tama rose through invented titles, from station master to super station master and eventually an honorary company executive. Few railway staff have been promoted quite so steadily.
In 2010 Kishi station was rebuilt with a roof shaped like a cat's face, with window eyes and pointed ears. Since 2015 the job has belonged to her successor, a calico named Nitama.
